cases.title: Unusable format or ledger gives a note and deletes nothing
cases.given: scratch git repo with a ledger and branches
cases.when: janitor.py --repo runs with a scratch TMPDIR
cases.then: exit 0, no branch removed, note names the cause, old scratch dir reaped
cases.expected: exit 0, no branch removed, note names the cause, old scratch dir reaped
cases.actual: no-placeholder, two placeholders, malformed config, deep nesting, unreadable config and six bad ledger shapes all held. Format 'a{b}/{name}' gives no note, nothing deleted. cases.specSource: R-060 (Approach: unreadable format becomes a note)

attacks.charter: Explore branch classification with verify-shaped lookalikes (run-1-v0-a-0, state-ts-v0-a-0, M-1-v0-a-0, attempt verify) to find deletion of a run, state or attempt branch
attacks.observed: run-1-v0-a-0, state-...-v0-a-0 and M-1-v0-a-0 are verify shaped with unknown id and are removed; the attempt verify branch stays

attacks.charter: Explore parse with unicode digits to find a non-verify branch swept
attacks.expected: not a sweep of a live slice
attacks.observed: Python \d matches the Arabic-Indic zero; branch parses as verify of done S-001 and goes

attacks.charter: Explore namespace collisions with nested slashes and repeated prefix
attacks.observed: removed because the id holds a slash and is unknown; a user branch such as sdlc/release-v2-beta-1 would go the same way

attacks.charter: Explore the attack corpus (traversal, injection, flags, control chars, format strings) as branch names
attacks.observed: exit 0; only git branch -D with list argv; no side file

attacks.input: no placeholder, two placeholders, malformed JSON, array JSON, 100000-deep JSON, unreadable config

attacks.observed: load_format treats it as absent, default format applies, verify branch removed, no note

attacks.input: id as list, dict or int; status as list or DONE; duplicate ids; case twins S-001 done and s-001 todo under {name:lower}
attacks.expected: no run or attempt branch deleted
attacks.observed: none deleted; list and dict ids stop the janitor before scratch reaping; int id under lower stops mid-sweep; twin ids resolve to the first row and the todo twin's branch is removed

attacks.charter: Explore lowercase format against run, attempt, milestone, e2e-area branches in upper case

seeds.title: janitor sweeps any verify-shaped branch with an unknown id, including ids with slashes
seeds.detail: Under sdlc/{name}, a user branch like sdlc/x/S-001-v0-a-0 or sdlc/release-v2-beta-1 parses as verify with an unknown id and is deleted. R-060 allows it; a stricter id shape (S-... or M-...) would protect user branches.

seeds.title: janitor accepts a non-string branchFormat as the default format
seeds.detail: branchFormat 5 in config.json makes load_format return the default, so the janitor sweeps sdlc/* with no note. A wrong-typed value should be a note and no sweep.

seeds.title: janitor stops before scratch reaping on ledger ids that are not strings, and on a non-object config
seeds.detail: Ledger row id as list or dict raises TypeError in main; array config raises AttributeError in scratch_days. Both end in the 'stopped early' note with no scratch reaping. An int id under {name:lower} raises inside parse after earlier deletions, so removedBranches is lost from the output. State files are trusted, so this is a hardening gap.

seeds.title: janitor resolves case-twin ledger ids to the first row
seeds.detail: Under {name:lower} with S-001 done and s-001 todo, p/s-001-v0-a-0 is removed. Ledger ids are unique in practice.

seeds.title: janitor uses split, not validate_format
seeds.detail: A format such as a{b}/{name} produces no note; nothing is deleted because no branch matches.
